records.summary: Planning, capacity building and project preparation for economic recovery in disaster-affected communities.
records.funding: Expected awards of $250,000–$500,000. Non-construction terms generally 12–18 months; Readiness projects may be shorter.
records.match: Generally up to 80% federal funding, with a 20% nonfederal share. EDA may set a different rate under the notice.
records.eligibility: Institutions of higher education may apply. Work must primarily benefit an area designated for a qualifying 2023 or 2024 disaster and directly engage its stakeholders. Primarily residential projects are generally ineligible. Apply through EDA EDGE.
records.condition: Requires an eligible disaster area and an economic-recovery purpose. University eligibility alone does not establish project eligibility.
notes: Readiness remains rolling until the notice is replaced, cancelled or funds are exhausted. This entry excludes the closed Industry Transformation Path.

records.program: FHIP Education and Outreach — General Component
records.summary: Local and regional education and outreach to prevent discriminatory housing practices.
records.funding: $175,000–$250,000 for the General Component; 12–18 months, with the final term negotiated by HUD.
records.match: No required match. Any voluntarily proposed match becomes binding if awarded.
records.eligibility: Eligible leads include public or private entities formulating or carrying out fair-housing programs. A university or partner must demonstrate this qualification and meet all notice requirements. Individuals are ineligible. This is an outreach program, not a general research award.
records.condition: The lead entity must qualify through fair-housing work. Funding cannot exceed 50% of the recipient organization’s annual operating budget.

records.summary: Independently conceived research on US housing and community development.
records.funding: No individual award minimum or maximum; approximately $2 million program pool. Project period negotiated with HUD.
records.match: At least 50% of total project cost (1:1 with HUD funds). Properly documented in-kind contributions may count.
records.eligibility: Colleges and universities are eligible organizational applicants. Submit a full research plan conceived independently of HUD solicitations; it must not duplicate federally funded work or repurpose another HUD competition proposal.
records.condition: University route requires the full match and independently developed housing research. Individual applications are ineligible.
